nodes.content: Design recoverable distributed snapshots for migrating stream operators with reordered messages and concurrent worker failures.
requirements: Recovery preserves a consistent cut and exactly-once outputs after any single worker crash.
Maintain at least 85% of snapshot-disabled throughput without globally pausing processing.

nodes.content: Use asynchronous sequence-fenced unaligned checkpoints with durable channel logs, atomic migration handoffs, and transactional sinks deduplicating epoch/sequence IDs.
How are late pre-fence records replayed exactly once when the old operator owner crashes before handoff commits?
Epoch-fenced successors replay pre-fence gaps from durable channel logs using checkpointed sequence watermarks, yielding zero duplicate commits after pre-handoff crashes.
Implement epoch-fenced handoffs and sequence-watermark replay; inject precommit owner crashes with reordered records, checking for duplicate commits.
Implement epoch-fenced replay; run HandoffChaos-1k with 1,000 precommit crashes and 5% reordering, comparing outputs and cuts against reference replay.
HandoffChaos-1k report containing reference-cut comparisons, duplicate-commit counts, and replay traces for 1,000 precommit crashes at 5% reordering.
Audit HandoffChaos-1k traces against reference cuts, counting duplicate commits and missed pre-fence records across all 1,000 crashes.
HandoffChaos-1k found zero duplicate commits and zero missed pre-fence records; all 1,000 recovered cuts matched reference replay.
Adopt epoch-fenced replay for precommit handoffs: HandoffChaos-1k matched all reference cuts with zero duplicate commits; benchmark throughput separately.
Run MoveBench-64 with 5% reordering, single-worker crashes, and 10 migrations/minute; compare throughput to snapshot-disabled baseline and measure global pauses.
MoveBench-64 sustained 79% of snapshot-disabled throughput at 10 migrations/minute, below the 85% target; channel-log flushes dominated stalls.
Asynchronous 4-ms log-flush batching with durability-gated acknowledgments preserves pre-fence replay after crashes and restores MoveBench-64 throughput to ≥85%.
Use HandoffChaos-1k crash traces to test 4-ms batched flushes with durability-gated acknowledgments; measure replay cuts, duplicate commits, and MoveBench-64 throughput.
With 4-ms batching, MoveBench-64 reached 87% baseline throughput; HandoffChaos-1k retained 1,000 matching cuts and zero duplicate commits.
Adopt durability-gated 4-ms channel-log batching: MoveBench-64 throughput rose from 79% to 87% without replay errors.
Use per-key MVCC snapshots and sequence-indexed replicated WAL, with passive shadow migration and transactional sink commits.
Implement MVCC/WAL shadow handoffs; verify reordered crash cuts and exactly-once outputs, then benchmark ≥85% MoveBench-64 throughput without global pauses.
Replay HandoffChaos-1k report traces through both designs; measure reference-cut matches, duplicate commits, MoveBench-64 throughput, and global pauses.
MVCC/WAL matched all 1,000 HandoffChaos-1k cuts with zero duplicate commits; MoveBench-64 reached 90% baseline throughput without global pauses.
Do simultaneous owner and shadow crashes preserve a recoverable cut and exactly-once sink commits beyond HandoffChaos-1k's single-crash coverage?
Third-replica-durable WAL acknowledgments and remote MVCC checkpoints preserve reference cuts and zero duplicate sink commits after simultaneous owner-shadow crashes.
Run DualCrash-500 with 500 simultaneous owner-shadow crashes and 5% reordering; check third-replica WAL recovery against reference cuts and sink commits.
DualCrash-500 found 3/500 mismatched cuts: shadow promotion raced remote MVCC checkpoint publication despite durable WAL; sink commits remained unique.
Gate epoch-fenced recovery on an atomically published MVCC manifest and WAL offset, predicting zero DualCrash-500 cut mismatches or duplicate commits.
Add atomic MVCC-manifest/WAL-offset publication before epoch-fenced promotion; rerun DualCrash-500 and compare cuts, duplicate commits, and MoveBench-64 throughput.
Atomic publication yielded 500/500 matching DualCrash-500 cuts, zero duplicate commits, and 89% snapshot-disabled throughput on MoveBench-64.
Inject single-worker crashes around atomic manifest publication and sink commits; verify reference cuts, output uniqueness, and pause time.
SingleCrash-Publish report containing crash traces, reference-cut comparisons, duplicate-output counts, and global-pause durations around publication and sink commits.
Use vector-clock cuts over broker-retained streams, lease-fenced migration, and transactional sinks keyed by input sequence.
How does a promoted owner detect missing causal predecessors across broker partitions when records reorder during a lease transition?
Replay SingleCrash-Publish traces across vector-clock lease transitions; compare broker-offset predecessor gaps, cut mismatches, and duplicate outputs against report.
On SingleCrash-Publish, broker-offset gap checks recovered every causal predecessor across 1,000 lease transitions; zero cut mismatches or duplicate outputs.
Select 89%-throughput atomic MVCC/WAL recovery and prototype broker-offset gap checks, which recovered predecessors across 1,000 lease transitions.
Integrate broker-offset gap checks into MVCC/WAL promotion; test reordered lease transitions, crash cuts, output uniqueness, and throughput against 85%.
Implement predecessor-gap checks at MVCC/WAL promotion; run 1,000 reordered single-crash transitions and MoveBench-64 at 10 migrations/minute.
GapCheck-1k report with predecessor-gap traces, reference-cut matches, duplicate-output counts, global-pause durations, and MoveBench-64 throughput.
Audit GapCheck-1k for reference-cut mismatches, duplicate outputs, and global pauses; compare MoveBench-64 throughput against the 85% floor.
GapCheck-1k matched all 1,000 reference cuts with zero duplicate outputs or global pauses; MoveBench-64 sustained 87% baseline throughput.
Record-attached dependency vectors and checkpointed broker offsets detect every cross-partition predecessor gap before promoted owners commit outputs.
Run CausalGap-2k on four partitions with 20% reordering and promotion crashes; compare vector-detected gaps against oracle causal histories.
CausalGap-2k missed 4 cross-partition gaps: migrated buffered records carried stale dependency vectors despite contiguous checkpointed offsets.
Replay GapCheck-1k buffered-record traces with injected stale dependency vectors; compare promotion gap detection against oracle predecessors and sink commits.
GapCheck-1k replay detected all 30 injected stale-vector gaps with noncontiguous checkpointed offsets before commits; CausalGap-2k misses remain.
How can promotion detect CausalGap-2k’s four stale-vector gaps hidden by contiguous offsets, unlike GapCheck-1k’s 30 detectable noncontiguous gaps?
Producer-stamped causal links in the broker log expose all four CausalGap-2k stale-vector gaps before promotion despite contiguous offsets.
Stamp broker records with producer causal links; rerun CausalGap-2k’s four contiguous-offset misses and GapCheck-1k’s 30 injections against oracle predecessors.
Producer-stamped links detected all four contiguous-offset CausalGap-2k gaps and all 30 GapCheck-1k injections before promotion.
Require producer-stamped causal links alongside offset checks: they caught four contiguous-offset misses and retained detection of 30 noncontiguous gaps.
Use quorum-published causal-frontier manifests, pipelined incremental state transfer, broker-log replay, and lease-fenced transactional sink epochs.
Implement pipelined frontier manifests and fenced sinks; validate reordered crash cuts, unique commits, and pause-free ≥85% MoveBench-64 throughput.
Using SingleCrash-Publish traces, implement quorum frontier publication and inject 1,000 owner crashes during pipelined transfers; compare cuts and sink commits.
FrontierCrash-1k report containing quorum-manifest histories, recovered-cut comparisons, sink-commit counts, and replay traces from 1,000 transfer-time crashes.
Audit FrontierCrash-1k cuts and sink commits against reference replay; benchmark p4 on MoveBench-64 for throughput and global pauses.
FrontierCrash-1k matched 1,000/1,000 reference cuts with zero duplicate commits; MoveBench-64 sustained 91% baseline throughput and zero global pauses.
Does validating producer-stamped causal links during frontier publication catch contiguous-offset gaps while preserving MoveBench-64 throughput above 85%?
Validating producer-stamped causal links before quorum publication catches all four contiguous-offset gaps while sustaining ≥85% MoveBench-64 throughput.
Add causal-link validation to FrontierCrash-1k manifests; replay four CausalGap-2k misses and benchmark MoveBench-64 throughput.
Causal-link validation caught all four contiguous-offset gaps, but MoveBench-64 throughput fell from 91% to 82%, below the 85% target.
Keep p4 experimental; optimize causal-link validation before adoption: baseline reaches 91%, but required gap checks reduce throughput to 82%.
Use vector-frontier microbatch checkpoints with indexed causal-link validation, replicated incremental state, and epoch-fenced transactional sinks.
Can indexed causal-link checks skip per-record lookups without missing stale-vector predecessors at microbatch boundaries?
Partition-level causal-link interval indexes validate microbatch frontier ranges without per-record lookups, detecting all four CausalGap-2k misses at ≥85% throughput.
Build causal-link interval indexes; test CausalGap-2k’s four misses at microbatch boundaries and measure MoveBench-64 throughput.
Interval indexes restored MoveBench-64 throughput to 88%, but missed one CausalGap-2k predecessor spanning a microbatch boundary.
Carry unresolved predecessor IDs across interval-index microbatches; validate boundary summaries before publication, predicting all four gap detections at ≥85% throughput.
Carry unresolved predecessor IDs between indexed microbatches; rerun four CausalGap-2k misses and MoveBench-64 throughput tests.
Boundary carryover detected all four CausalGap-2k misses; MoveBench-64 sustained 86% baseline throughput.
Integrate boundary carryover into p5; validate reordered single-crash recovery, cut consistency, exactly-once commits, and ≥85% throughput.
Replay FrontierCrash-1k traces through p5 with boundary carryover, checking reference cuts, duplicate commits, global pauses, and MoveBench-64 throughput.
BoundaryFrontier-1k report with recovered-cut comparisons, duplicate-commit counts, global-pause durations, and MoveBench-64 throughput under boundary carryover.
Audit BoundaryFrontier-1k for cut mismatches, duplicate commits, global pauses, and MoveBench-64 throughput against the 85% target.
BoundaryFrontier-1k matched all 1,000 recovered cuts, with zero duplicate commits or global pauses; MoveBench-64 sustained 86% baseline throughput.
Adopt p5 with boundary carryover: four gaps caught, 1,000 matching cuts, zero duplicate commits or global pauses, 86% throughput.
Choose p5: producer-stamped causal checks sustain 86%; p1 and p2 lack validation, while validated p4 falls from 91% to 82%.
